body:
This duration should be exposed as a project setting, so you can adjust it for accessibility reasons. Check the implementation of the `"gui/timers/incremental_search_max_interval_msec"` project setting across the codebase for a reference.

Also, the default duration feels a bit long. It might be worth trying to reduce it to 0.5 seconds, but I don't know if this will have adverse effects on a trackpad or touch input (Android editor). I'll let others confirm this first though.

Oh thanks for bringing that up, I meant to ask about it. I used https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/41138 as a reference for this, and I figured it'd be good for both unfolding behaviors to share a timing configuration. I just wasn't sure where to put it. I'll add that and connect it to the tree and the inspector :+1:

I saw some code that lead me to believe that drag-n-drop is disabled for touch interactions, but I may have misread. Disabling drag-n-drop does seem like an egregious mis-use of the touch medium, now that I think about it, so I probably did misread.

Actually... I'm thinking this should be an editor setting, not a project setting, and ~add a parameter to the tree~ add a theme variable to control it. (the editor's theme would get the editor setting on startup) (I haven't verified yet that my mental model of how the editor works is compatible with this plan, but I will try it shortly)

If users of the Tree node want trees to have different hover times for some reason, it would allow that. It would also allow different collaborators of the same godot project to have their own settings, which is more accessible.

body:
I made it a regular property at first. But that means every tree in the godot editor needs to get the property set, while also not setting it on trees in user space. So either all the contexts which create a tree need to set this to the config value, or we need a subclass of tree for the editor to use.
I figured doing it with a theme variable was more ergonomic both in this codebase and for users' trees, even though it does feel odd. And unfortunate that theme variables don't have a float option. But tree also has a theme property called `scroll_speed` so I felt ok about it.
I can change to one of the other options though if that's preferred.

body: It can go into `interface/editor` probably.

```suggestion
	EDITOR_SETTING_USAGE(Variant::BOOL, PROPERTY_HINT_NONE, "interface/inspector/auto_unfold_foreign_scenes", true, "", PROPERTY_USAGE_DEFAULT | PROPERTY_USAGE_RESTART_IF_CHANGED)
```

This should probably stop the Timer.
Unlikely that someone will run into this, but if you disable the property while hovering, it would still unfold.

You are passing the time to `start()`, so setting it here is unnecessary.
Also you should enable `one_shot` for the Timer (it's off by default).
I'll check if it's enabled in the timer callback too, that'll be nice and robust
This should be cached IMO, this is fetch is not free
